bc



Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc-parallel test "PTP Slave Clock Sync" timed out unable to detect a LOCKED OS clock because a test-code change in k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator commit d20ffcbf0c (July 3, 2026) introduced a key collision bug in createStoredEvent that silently drops the notification state from received CloudEvents.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: Key collision in createStoredEvent drops LOCKED notification state (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

[event.go: 730] Context Attributes,

type: event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change

source: /sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state

Data,

{"version":"1.0","values":[

{"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},

{"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-2"}

]}

[event.go: 734] Latency for the event: 36942 ms

[ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state ... eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-2]]

[ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000

[ptp.go: 393] [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```


• Root Cause: Commit d20ffcbf0c on k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator (merged 2026-07-03, title: "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed createStoredEvent in test/pkg/event/event.go (v2 path, line 730) to use v.Resource (ResourceAddress) as the StoredEventValues map key instead of v.DataType. For os-clock-sync-state-change events, both DataValues — the notification ("LOCKED") and the metric (-2) — share the same ResourceAddress (/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME), so the second loop iteration (metric) silently overwrites the first (notification). The resulting map has no "notification" key, so testSyncState in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–414 always reads state = "" and wasLocked never becomes true. The clock hardware was actually LOCKED (confirmed by the raw CloudEvent data), but the test could not detect it and timed out after 5 minutes per {Enable:true FailureThreshold:1 Duration:5} config. This is a test-code regression on main — the production release-4.22 images are unaffected.

• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c on k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator main (2026-07-03) — https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/commit/d20ffcbf0c

• Is it a flake? No — the key collision is deterministic and will fail on every run until fixed.

• Suggested Fix: In test/pkg/event/event.go createStoredEvent v2 path, restore v.DataType as the map key for each DataValue (reverting the key change from d20ffcbf0c). To also support the multiple-metric BC clock-class use case that motivated the change, either accumulate values into a slice or use a composite key like "/" and update all callers that read values["notification"] and values["metric"] accordingly.

Suite Issue Class: test_regression

Suite Severity: HIGH

Root Cause Groups:

For os-clock-sync-state-change events, both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric (-2) DataValues share the same ResourceAddress (/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. ptp.go:414 then reads values["notification"] as "" (key absent), wasLocked never becomes true, and the test times out after 5 minutes. The clock hardware was confirmed LOCKED in raw CloudEvent data — this is a test-code regression only; production release-4.22 images are unaffected.


Cross-Suite Patterns:


• All suites share the same root cause (bc, oc, and per the oc analysis also dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha). The failure is systematic and code-level: every suite running Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync hits the same bad key lookup path in testSyncState. No suite-specific variation is present — the clockOffset=0.000000 debug output (instead of the expected metric value) appears in both analyzed suites identically, confirming the key-mismatch affects both the notification and metric reads.

• Suggested Fix: In test/pkg/event/event.go createStoredEvent v2 path, restore v.DataType as the map key for each DataValue (reverting the key change from d20ffcbf0c). To also support the multiple-metric BC clock-class use case that motivated the change, either accumulate values into a slice or use a composite key like "/" and update all callers that read values["notification"] and values["metric"] accordingly.

Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp



TL;DR: linuxptp-daemon PR #618 broke T-GM holdover and T-BC sync (9 failures); a test-code key regression in d20ffcb broke all 5 parallel event tests (5 failures).



Root Cause Groups


#FailuresSuitesRoot Cause
19 / 15tbc (×6), tgm (×3)openshift/linuxptp-daemon PR #618 (d2ff2d154d, merged release-4.22 2026-06-30): T-GM holdover state machine bypassed — class 7 never emitted, jumps LOCKED (6) → FREERUN (248) directly; T-BC on cnfdf32 consequently stuck in FREERUN (class 248) with phc2sys never starting, cascading to all 6 tbc serial tests.
25 / 15bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc (all -parallel)Test-code regression commit d20ffcb (Jul 3, 2026, main): createStoredEvent in test/pkg/event/event.go changed the values-map key from DataType ("notification") to ResourceAddress; testSyncState() still looks up values["notification"], always gets nil, wasLocked never becomes true. All 5 parallel suites ran concurrently, all timed out at ≈363 s (ptp.go:393). Secondary contributor: cloud-event-proxy:release-4.22 sidecar and/or the shared consumer pod in ptp-event-framework-test may not have been serving OsClockSyncStateChange events during the parallel window (PushInitialEvent exhausted all 30 × 10 s retries).
31 / 15dualnicbcha (serial)phc2sys HA failover — phc2sys did not switch to secondary ptp4l after the primary interface was downed, or failed to emit the expected log line. Likely a cascade of the T-BC FREERUN state from Group 1.


Cross-Suite Patterns


• tbc + tgm share one root cause (PR #618): T-GM FREERUN propagates upstream — T-BC has no grandmaster to lock to, leaving cnfdf32 in class 248 and making all T-BC serial tests deterministically fail. Fixing PR #618 unblocks both suites.
• All 5 parallel suites share one root cause (commit d20ffcb): bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and oc fail with identical timing (≈363 s) and identical failure message, confirming a single shared code path broken by the same commit.
• dualnicbcha is the only suite with failures from two separate groups (1 parallel event + 1 serial HA), making it appear to have the most diverse failure set.
• No suite-specific flakes — every failure traces to one of the two breaking changes above.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Revert or patch openshift/linuxptp-daemon PR #618 on release-4.22 — restore the T-GM holdover servo-state path so ts2phc emits clock class 7 before transitioning to 248, and re-add the FREERUN ptp-state-change CloudEvent dispatch in the restarted-ts2phc code path. This is the highest-leverage fix: 9/15 failures resolved.

2. Fix the createStoredEvent key regression from commit d20ffcb in test/pkg/event/event.go (runs from main) — update the consumer in ptp.go:413–414 to use the new ResourceAddress-keyed lookup (e.g., values[resourceAddress].(string)) instead of values["notification"], or revert the key to DataType. Also pin CONSUMER_IMG to a versioned tag instead of :latest to prevent silent consumer regressions. 5/15 failures resolved.

3. Add a guard in tbc test AfterEach to restore the original ptpConfig even on failure — this prevents the cascade from Group 1 (nil ptpConfig) from adding spurious secondary failures when the primary T-BC issue recurs.


Overall Issue Class: test_failure (production image regression in release-4.22 + test-code regression on main)


Overall Severity: CRITICAL — 15/15 failures, every suite affected, PTP synchronization infrastructure completely non-functional for both T-GM and T-BC hardware paths.

For os-clock-sync-state-change events, both DataValues — the notification ("LOCKED") and the metric (-2) — share the same ResourceAddress (/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME), so the second loop iteration (metric) silently overwrites the first (notification). For os-clock-sync-state-change events, both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric (-2) DataValues share the same ResourceAddress (/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME), so the metric entry silently overwrites the notification entry. ptp.go:414 then reads values["notification"] as "" (key absent), wasLocked never becomes true, and the test times out after 5 minutes. The clock hardware was confirmed LOCKED in raw CloudEvent data — this is a test-code regression only; production release-4.22 images are unaffected.


Cross-Suite Patterns:


• All suites share the same root cause (bc, oc, and per the oc analysis also dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha). The failure is systematic and code-level: every suite running Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync hits the same bad key lookup path in testSyncState. No suite-specific variation is present — the clockOffset=0.000000 debug output (instead of the expected metric value) appears in both analyzed suites identically, confirming the key-mismatch affects both the notification and metric reads.


Actionable Recommendations:


1. Revert the map key change in createStoredEvent (test/pkg/event/event.go, v2 path, ~line 730): restore v.DataType as the key for each DataValue loop iteration, undoing the d20ffcbf0c change. This directly fixes all 15 failures across every suite.

2. Add a regression test for createStoredEvent that asserts the returned map contains both "notification" and "metric" keys when given a dual-DataValue os-clock-sync-state-change event — preventing future key changes from silently breaking event parsing.

3. Block the PR that introduced d20ffcbf0c (or open a revert PR) against k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator main immediately, as every nightly run on this job will continue to fail 100% of the time until the fix lands.


Overall Issue Class: test_regression


Overall Severity: HIGH — all 15 test failures trace to a single deterministic code regression on main; no hardware or infra issues involved, but the entire nightly job is broken on every run until resolved.




Per-Suite Details



bc



Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc-parallel test "PTP Slave Clock Sync" timed out unable to detect a LOCKED OS clock because a test-code change in k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator commit d20ffcbf0c (July 3, 2026) introduced a key collision bug in createStoredEvent that silently drops the notification state from received CloudEvents.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: Key collision in createStoredEvent drops LOCKED notification state (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

[event.go: 730] Context Attributes,

type: event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change

source: /sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state

Data,

{"version":"1.0","values":[

{"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},

{"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-2"}

]}

[event.go: 734] Latency for the event: 36942 ms

[ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state ... eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-2]]

[ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000

[ptp.go: 393] [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```


• Root Cause: Commit d20ffcbf0c on k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator (merged 2026-07-03, title: "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") changed createStoredEvent in test/pkg/event/event.go (v2 path, line 730) to use v.Resource (ResourceAddress) as the StoredEventValues map key instead of v.DataType. For os-clock-sync-state-change events, both DataValues — the notification ("LOCKED") and the metric (-2) — share the same ResourceAddress (/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME), so the second loop iteration (metric) silently overwrites the first (notification). The resulting map has no "notification" key, so testSyncState in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–414 always reads state = "" and wasLocked never becomes true. The clock hardware was actually LOCKED (confirmed by the raw CloudEvent data), but the test could not detect it and timed out after 5 minutes per {Enable:true FailureThreshold:1 Duration:5} config. This is a test-code regression on main — the production release-4.22 images are unaffected.

• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c on k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator main (2026-07-03) — https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/commit/d20ffcbf0c

• Is it a flake? No — the key collision is deterministic and will fail on every run until fixed.

• Suggested Fix: In test/pkg/event/event.go createStoredEvent v2 path, restore v.DataType as the map key for each DataValue (reverting the key change from d20ffcbf0c). To also support the multiple-metric BC clock-class use case that motivated the change, either accumulate values into a slice or use a composite key like "/" and update all callers that read values["notification"] and values["metric"] accordingly.

Suite Issue Class: test_regression

Suite Severity: HIGH

TL;DR: A main-branch test key-naming regression breaks all 6 parallel event-sync tests; 4 tgm-serial failures stem from unported daemon features.



Root Cause Groups:


• ~6/16 failures — createStoredEvent() key-change regression breaks testSyncState() in all parallel suites ([bc-parallel], [dualfollower-parallel], [dualnicbc-parallel], [dualnicbcha-parallel], [oc-parallel], [tbc-parallel] — all: Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

Commit d20ffcb (2026-07-03) / PR #711 commit 5e9ecf0 (2026-07-15) changed createStoredEvent() in test/pkg/event/event.go to store values under v.Resource (e.g. /cluster/node/…/CLOCK_REALTIME) instead of v.DataType ("notification"). testSyncState() in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go still reads values["notification"].(string) — that key is now always absent. state is permanently "", wasLocked never flips, and every parallel event suite exhausts its configured window (~6 min) and fails deterministically at ptp.go:393.


• 1/16 failures — ts2phc process_restart_count reset on PtpConfig delete/re-apply ([tgm-serial] Verify ts2phc metrics are cleaned up after GM PtpConfig delete and re-apply)

Commit be1eb0d3 (2026-06-28) added a main-only CI test asserting the restart counter is monotonically non-decreasing across a delete/re-apply cycle. The linuxptp-daemon unconditionally deletes the CounterVec label set in DeleteProcessStatusMetrics (cleanup.go:58), resetting the counter to 1. The corresponding daemon fix does not exist in release-4.22 or main, so the assertion fails every run.


• 3/16 failures — T-GM ClockClass 7 holdover window too brief for detection ([tgm-serial] "Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss", "Continuously terminating ts2phc triggers FREERUN event and then recovers to LOCKED", "Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery")

After GNSS disable, the hardware transitions through ClockClass 7 (holdover) transiently before reaching 248 (FREERUN). The polling interval and event-window size in the main-branch test code are too coarse to catch this transition against release-4.22 images, which may move through holdover more quickly than assumed. By the time the test polls, ptp4l is already at class 248.


• ~6/16 failures — origin unclear from provided analyses (may be additional serial failures or unanalyzed suite variants)


Cross-Suite Patterns:


PatternSuites affectedSuite-specific?
values["notification"] key mismatchbc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc (all parallel)No — cross-suite, same root cause

All 6 parallel suites share a single root cause (the key-change regression in test/pkg/event/event.go). Serial suites in bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, oc passed their clock-sync tests — confirming PTP hardware sync was functional and only the event-reporting/test-parsing path was broken. The tgm failures are entirely independent and suite-specific.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Fix testSyncState() in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go (highest impact — unblocks ~6 failures): Update the values["notification"] and values["metric"] lookups to use the ResourceAddress key emitted by cloud-event-proxy (e.g. look up by iterating the map or by a named constant matching the resource path format), or add a GetValueByDataType(dataType) helper in test/pkg/event/event.go so all consumers are decoupled from the raw key format. This single change restores all 6 parallel event-based suites.

2. Gate the ts2phc restart-count test behind a daemon capability check or skip it on release-4.22 (fixes 1 failure): The test in ptp.go:2628 was merged to main before the linuxptp-daemon fix exists. Either implement and cherry-pick the daemon-side counter-preservation fix to release-4.22, or add a version/feature guard so the assertion is skipped when running against images that do not support it.

3. Extend T-GM ClockClass 7 detection polling in tgm serial tests (fixes 3 failures): Increase the poll interval tolerance or use event-based detection (subscribing to ClockClassChange events) rather than log-polling to observe the holdover transition. The current test assumes a minimum holdover window that release-4.22 images do not guarantee.

The fact that all 6 parallel suites fail the same event-based clock sync test simultaneously while all bc serial tests pass is the defining signal: this is a cross-mode systemic PTP environment instability, not a bc-specific code regression. A relevant contextual factor is commit 4aa5310 (ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent, Aug 2025) which notes that OCPBUGS-60570 changed when OsClockSyncStateChange events can be pulled from the socket — this fix is on main (test code), but the release-4.22 production images may have that bug fix applied, meaning the event socket behavior is correct; the issue is the underlying clock sync state at test time.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no check_backport.py available and repos are shallow main-branch clones; the cross-suite pattern points to a transient PTP environment condition rather than a specific code commit. Related context: OCPBUGS-60570 (event socket behavior, fixed in 4aa5310 on main).

• Is it a flake? yes — The simultaneous failure of all 6 parallel PTP Slave Clock Sync tests while all serial bc tests pass is the hallmark of a transient PTP grandmaster or GPS-signal instability causing all downstream clocks to remain in FREERUN during the parallel test window. The [tgm-serial] test suite also shows failures for WPC GM GNSS signal loss tests and ts2phc termination tests (which intentionally disrupt the grandmaster), and the 5-minute test window is narrow enough that a temporary GPS/upstream disruption could prevent all parallel suites from observing a LOCKED transition.

• Suggested Fix: Re-run the periodic job to confirm this is a transient flake. If it recurs consistently, check the cloud-event-proxy sidecar logs on release-4.22 images for FREERUN/HOLDOVER reasons, and verify whether the GNSS/TGM disruption tests in [tgm-serial] are sharing timing infrastructure with the BC test nodes.

Suite TL;DR: The single "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync" failure is a deterministic test regression introduced by commit d20ffcb on main (July 3, 2026), which broke how PTP sync-state events are looked up in the test's key-value store, causing all parallel-mode suites to never detect a LOCKED clock state.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: createStoredEvent key-change regression breaks values["notification"] lookup (affects: [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• JUnit result: "[It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.898387443, "result": "error"} — test ran its full ~6-minute configured duration before dying.
• investigation-summary.txt: Source: ptp.go:393 → which is Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393.
• Same test fails in all parallel suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc) in junit-failures.txt, confirming a systematic rather than per-mode cause.
• From commit d20ffcb diff (test/pkg/event/event.go, lines 711–716 and 742–751 as shipped):

```go

// Use ResourceAddress as key to avoid collisions…

key := v.Resource // e.g. "/cluster/node1/ptp/CLOCK_REALTIME"

if key == "" {

key = string(v.DataType)

}

values[key] = v.Value

```

• cloud-event-proxy/plugins/ptp_operator/metrics/manager.go:319–324 always sets Resource: eventSource (non-empty path like /cluster/node1/ptp/CLOCK_REALTIME) and DataType: NOTIFICATION for the sync-state value.
• test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go testSyncState() reads: state, _ := values["notification"].(string) — this key is now never populated because the storage key is the resource path, not "notification". wasLocked stays false for the full test duration.
• CI build log confirms TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts are from main, which includes d20ffcb.
• Root Cause: Commit d20ffcb (July 3, 2026) refactored createStoredEvent in test/pkg/event/event.go to use v.Resource as the map key (to handle BC-mode multi-instance collisions), but the cloud-event-proxy always emits a non-empty Resource field (a full cluster resource path). The existing testSyncState in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go still reads values["notification"] (the old DataType-based key), which is now empty for every event. Consequently, state is always "", wasLocked never flips to true, and the test exhausts its 6-minute window before failing at ptp.go:393.
• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcb (CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash) — merged main 2026-07-03. Not cherry-picked to release-4.22; this is purely a test-code regression on main.
• Is it a flake? No — deterministic. The storage key change is unconditional; the lookup mismatch will reproduce on every run with this test binary.
• Suggested Fix: In testSyncState (and any other consumer of StoredEventValues), replace values["notification"] with a lookup that iterates over the map looking for a value whose key ends in CLOCK_REALTIME (or reconstruct the expected resource path), OR revert the createStoredEvent key strategy for notification values to keep string(v.DataType) as the key and use a qualified key only for METRIC values where collision is the actual concern.

Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp


TL;DR: Hardware sync failures across RDU2 nodes and a deterministic PMC split-args code bug together account for 36 test failures spanning all 7 suites.



Root Cause Groups


#DescriptionCountSuites
1T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN on cnfdf32 — DPLL shows LOCKED but ts2phc reports FREERUN; daemon gate blocks phc2sys, clockClass never reaches 6, cascading to event/metric/holdover failures11 / 36tgm
2BC slave port ens2f0np0 / hardware clock sync degradation — BC slave stuck in MASTER state; ptp4l clockClass stuck at 248 (FREERUN) on dualnicbc nodes; cascading to config, event-consumer, and interface-recovery tests~14 / 36dualnicbc (5–6), dualnicbcha (8–9)
3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)
4Parallel event soak test timeout (OCPBUGS-60570 interaction) — PushInitialEvent retry loop (up to 30 × 10 s = 300 s) shares the same 6-minute soak timer; release-5.0 image fix (OCPBUGS-60570) slows initial event delivery, exhausting the budget before LOCKED is received; all 5 parallel suites hit this simultaneously pointing to a cluster-wide event delivery slowdown5 / 36bc (1), dualfollower (1), oc (1), dualnicbc (1), dualnicbcha (1)
5No T-BC topology on cluster — CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry finds 0 T-BC L2 solutions on cnfdf30–32; execute.BeforeAll calls Fail() instead of Skip(), failing the first spec and silently skipping the rest1 / 36tbc


Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.

dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite



Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp


TL;DR: Hardware sync failures across RDU2 nodes and a deterministic PMC split-args code bug together account for 36 test failures spanning all 7 suites.



Root Cause Groups


#DescriptionCountSuites
1T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN on cnfdf32 — DPLL shows LOCKED but ts2phc reports FREERUN; daemon gate blocks phc2sys, clockClass never reaches 6, cascading to event/metric/holdover failures11 / 36tgm
2BC slave port ens2f0np0 / hardware clock sync degradation — BC slave stuck in MASTER state; ptp4l clockClass stuck at 248 (FREERUN) on dualnicbc nodes; cascading to config, event-consumer, and interface-recovery tests~14 / 36dualnicbc (5–6), dualnicbcha (8–9)
3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)
4Parallel event soak test timeout (OCPBUGS-60570 interaction) — PushInitialEvent retry loop (up to 30 × 10 s = 300 s) shares the same 6-minute soak timer; release-5.0 image fix (OCPBUGS-60570) slows initial event delivery, exhausting the budget before LOCKED is received; all 5 parallel suites hit this simultaneously pointing to a cluster-wide event delivery slowdown5 / 36bc (1), dualfollower (1), oc (1), dualnicbc (1), dualnicbcha (1)
5No T-BC topology on cluster — CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry finds 0 T-BC L2 solutions on cnfdf30–32; execute.BeforeAll calls Fail() instead of Skip(), failing the first spec and silently skipping the rest1 / 36tbc


Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.



Overall Issue Class


infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.

Suite Issue Class: test_flake

dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite



Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp


TL;DR: Hardware sync failures across RDU2 nodes and a deterministic PMC split-args code bug together account for 36 test failures spanning all 7 suites.



Root Cause Groups


#DescriptionCountSuites
1T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN on cnfdf32 — DPLL shows LOCKED but ts2phc reports FREERUN; daemon gate blocks phc2sys, clockClass never reaches 6, cascading to event/metric/holdover failures11 / 36tgm
2BC slave port ens2f0np0 / hardware clock sync degradation — BC slave stuck in MASTER state; ptp4l clockClass stuck at 248 (FREERUN) on dualnicbc nodes; cascading to config, event-consumer, and interface-recovery tests~14 / 36dualnicbc (5–6), dualnicbcha (8–9)
3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)
4Parallel event soak test timeout (OCPBUGS-60570 interaction) — PushInitialEvent retry loop (up to 30 × 10 s = 300 s) shares the same 6-minute soak timer; release-5.0 image fix (OCPBUGS-60570) slows initial event delivery, exhausting the budget before LOCKED is received; all 5 parallel suites hit this simultaneously pointing to a cluster-wide event delivery slowdown5 / 36bc (1), dualfollower (1), oc (1), dualnicbc (1), dualnicbcha (1)
5No T-BC topology on cluster — CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry finds 0 T-BC L2 solutions on cnfdf30–32; execute.BeforeAll calls Fail() instead of Skip(), failing the first spec and silently skipping the rest1 / 36tbc


Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.



Overall Issue Class


infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.

Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reported LOCKED via PTP events within test duration (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite

All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.

Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. • The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.

Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite

Cross-Suite Patterns

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. If this is reproducible, raise a bug against the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy image referencing OCPBUGS-60570 and confirm the fix is correctly backported.

Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp


TL;DR: Hardware sync failures across RDU2 nodes and a deterministic PMC split-args code bug together account for 36 test failures spanning all 7 suites.



Root Cause Groups


#DescriptionCountSuites
1T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN on cnfdf32 — DPLL shows LOCKED but ts2phc reports FREERUN; daemon gate blocks phc2sys, clockClass never reaches 6, cascading to event/metric/holdover failures11 / 36tgm
2BC slave port ens2f0np0 / hardware clock sync degradation — BC slave stuck in MASTER state; ptp4l clockClass stuck at 248 (FREERUN) on dualnicbc nodes; cascading to config, event-consumer, and interface-recovery tests~14 / 36dualnicbc (5–6), dualnicbcha (8–9)
3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)
4Parallel event soak test timeout (OCPBUGS-60570 interaction) — PushInitialEvent retry loop (up to 30 × 10 s = 300 s) shares the same 6-minute soak timer; release-5.0 image fix (OCPBUGS-60570) slows initial event delivery, exhausting the budget before LOCKED is received; all 5 parallel suites hit this simultaneously pointing to a cluster-wide event delivery slowdown5 / 36bc (1), dualfollower (1), oc (1), dualnicbc (1), dualnicbcha (1)
5No T-BC topology on cluster — CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry finds 0 T-BC L2 solutions on cnfdf30–32; execute.BeforeAll calls Fail() instead of Skip(), failing the first spec and silently skipping the rest1 / 36tbc


Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.



Overall Issue Class


infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.

Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc failure is the event-based PTP Slave Clock Sync test timing out because the OS clock never reached LOCKED state (as reported via PTP events) within the test's monitoring window.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reported LOCKED via PTP events within test duration (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. If this is reproducible, raise a bug against the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy image referencing OCPBUGS-60570 and confirm the fix is correctly backported.

Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

to equal : 6

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite

1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Suite TL;DR: The single parallel event-based clock-sync test failed because the OS clock never achieved LOCKED state within the test timeout, a pattern shared with 4 other parallel suites in the same run — indicating a systemic PTP hardware lock issue on the test infrastructure.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reached LOCKED state (event-based soak test timeout) (affects: [It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• "[It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.725084115, "result": "error"} (from telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json)
• Test: [It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync\n Message: result: error (from junit-failures.txt)
• The identical failure appears in 4 other parallel suites in the same job: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync, [It] [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync, [It] [dualnicbcha-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync, [It] [oc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync
• From junit-failures.txt: dualnicbc-serial also fails PTP ClockSync: [It] [dualnicbc-serial] PTP e2e tests PTP ClockSync Slave can sync to master [Serial]: result: error — confirming the hardware PTP chain itself was not syncing during the run.
• Job: Container test exited with code 1, reason Error at 05:21:35Z (ci-operator-build-log.txt).
• Root Cause: The test testSyncState() in test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and fails at line 393 with Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") when the test-case duration timer fires before the clock ever reports a LOCKED state. The test ran for ~363 seconds without ever receiving a LOCKED event. The simultaneous failure of the same event-based test across all 5 parallel suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc), plus serial PTP-sync failures in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha/tgm/tbc suites in the same run, points to the PTP grandmaster-to-slave synchronization chain being degraded or disconnected on the RDU2 test hardware during this job window rather than any code regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no code change identified; this is a hardware/infrastructure timing failure. Test code on main already includes commit 4aa5310 (ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent) which extended PushInitialEvent retries to 30×10s for exactly this class of slow-start scenario. The release-5.0 images are built from release-5.0 branch. No new cherry-pick or release-5.0 code change identified as a trigger.
• Is it a flake? yes — simultaneous failure across 5 independent parallel suites on the same hardware node pool at the same wall-clock time is the hallmark of a transient infra condition (PTP GM link loss, NIC reset, or environmental timing glitch), not a reproducible code defect. The dualfollower serial suite's configuration-verification tests all passed in the same run.
• Suggested Fix: Re-run the job to confirm this is transient. If it recurs, check whether the PTP grandmaster at cnfdf30/cnfdf31/cnfdf32 (RDU2 telco5g lab) was in holdover or FREERUN during the test window by examining the must-gather artifacts and pod-logs collected at post-step; longer-term, the test could be made more resilient by retrying the entire soak test when zero LOCKED events are observed within the first few minutes.
